# Suite resume, Retry of a failed feature, and Start integration

## What to build

`graph-execution suite` already runs features as child runs; its orchestrator is `runSuite` in `src/suite/orchestrator.ts`. Its state lives in `<suiteDir>/suite.json` (`SuiteStore` and the schemas are in `src/suite/state.ts`):
- each feature has `name`, `tasksDir`, `prd`, `runId`, `status` (`queued | running | done | failed | stopped | excluded`), `share`, `pid`, `exitCode` and `finishedAt`;
- the suite `status` is one of `running | integrating | applied | done | failed | aborted`.

This slice adds three things.

1. **`graph-execution suite --resume [--run <suite-id>]`.** It finds the suite folder (the latest `suite-*` folder with a `suite.json` when no id is given) and takes its lock. For every feature that is not `done` or `excluded`, it restarts the feature under the same queue and cap rules:
   - resume the feature's run (`--resume --run <runId>`) when `<suiteDir>/features/<runId>/state.json` exists;
   - otherwise start it fresh with the same pre-generated `runId`.

   Then it continues as a normal suite.

2. **Retry of a failed feature, while other features still run.** A `SuiteControl` object (modeled on `RetryHub`) accepts requests from outside; the web page in a later slice will call it. `retryFeature(name)` restarts a `failed` feature by resuming its run. It takes a free slot with share 1, or is queued if none is free.

3. **Start integration.** When nothing is running or queued, at least one feature is `done` and at least one is `failed`, the orchestrator waits on the control. `startIntegration()` marks the failed features `excluded` and moves on to the phase after the features. That phase doesn't exist yet: for now the suite ends `done` with exit 0, and the log lists the excluded features. Without a control (foreground, no web page), the suite ends as today, `failed` with exit 2, and prints `run graph-execution suite --resume to retry the failed features`.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `src/suite/orchestrator.ts`: `runSuite`, the start loop with `initialShares`, the exit handling (reads `state.json` `status` of the child run), and stop handling.
- `src/suite/spawn.ts`: `SpawnFeature`, `FeatureProcess`, `featureArgs`.
- `src/suite/state.ts`: `SuiteStore`, `suiteStateSchema`, `SUITE_FILE`, `suiteDirOf`, `featureRunDir`.
- `src/state/paths.ts`: `RUNS_ROOT_ENV`, `RUN_ID_ENV`. A resume child needs `GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUNS_ROOT=<suiteDir>/features` so that `--resume --run <runId>` finds its folder. Don't set `RUN_ID_ENV` for a resume.
- `src/runner/retry-hub.ts` (lines 13-133): the `RetryHub` pattern to mirror. It has `wait`, `retryNode` returning `{ok} | {ok: false, reason}`, `quit`, `onChange`, and `whenWaiting` for tests.
- `src/launch/preflight.ts` (lines 139-166): `preflightResume` refuses a resume when the spec, tasks or config changed (hash check). A resumed feature child can therefore fail with that message. Treat it as a feature failure.
- `src/state/resume.ts` (lines 22-33): the `findRun` pattern for "latest folder by sorted name".
- `src/state/state.ts`: `acquireLock`, `lockHolder`.
- `src/cli.ts`: the `suite` subcommand registration (`--feature`, `--provider`, `--model`, `--concurrency`, `--no-merge`). The root command declares `--resume` and `--run` too, so read them as `opts.x ?? program.opts<RunOptions>().x`.
- `src/suite/orchestrator.test.ts`: existing helpers (fixture copy, failing fake script, stop test) to reuse.

## Patterns to follow

**RetryHub shape** (src/runner/retry-hub.ts):
```ts
export type RetryResult = { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: "not_waiting" | "not_retryable" | "not_mergeable" };
retryNode(id: string): RetryResult { ... resolve the pending wait ... }
quit(): void { this.quitted = true; ... }
```

**Event-driven wait:** the orchestrator loop races children exits **and** the next control request:
```ts
await Promise.race([...running.map((r) => r.exited.then(() => ({ exit: r.name }))), control.next()]);
```

## Step-by-step tasks

### CREATE `src/suite/control.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**:
  ```ts
  export type SuiteRequest = { retry: string } | { integrate: true };
  export type ControlResult = { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: "not_failed" | "not_ready" | "unknown" };
  export class SuiteControl {
    /** Set by the orchestrator: what is currently allowed. */
    setAllowed(a: { retry: string[]; integrate: boolean }): void;
    get allowed(): { retry: string[]; integrate: boolean };
    retryFeature(name: string): ControlResult;   // ok only if name is in allowed.retry
    startIntegration(): ControlResult;           // ok only if allowed.integrate
    next(): Promise<SuiteRequest | undefined>;   // resolves with the next accepted request; undefined after quit()
    quit(): void;
    onChange(fn: () => void): () => void;
  }
  ```
  Accepted requests go into a queue, and `next()` takes from it.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/suite/control.test.ts` (write unit tests: refused when not allowed, accepted requests come out of `next()` in order, `quit` resolves a pending `next()` with `undefined`).

### UPDATE `src/suite/orchestrator.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - Split `runSuite` into `startSuite(opts)` (validate, create the folder and `suite.json`) and `driveFeatures(ctx, opts)`, the loop. Also add `resumeSuite({cwd, suiteId?, control?, spawn?, cliPath?, log?, signal?})`:
    - `resumeSuite` finds the suite with `findSuite(repo, id?)`. That function lists `.graph-execution/suite-*` folders that have `suite.json`, sorted, and takes the last. Its errors are `no suite <id> to resume in <dir>` and `no suite to resume in <dir>`.
    - It refuses a suite whose status is `applied` or `done` with `suite <id> already finished`.
    - It acquires the lock (a `LockError` when live) and sets suite status `running`. Features that are `running` or `stopped` go back to `queued`. Features that are `failed` stay `failed` but are restarted at once as resumes, so a plain `--resume` retries them.
    - Then it calls `driveFeatures`.
  - In `driveFeatures`, a feature start is either `fresh` (`featureArgs` plus `RUN_ID_ENV`) or `resume` (`["--resume", "--run", runId]`, plus `--concurrency` is **not** accepted on resume, so pass nothing else). The resume always sets `RUNS_ROOT_ENV`.
    - On resume, the run keeps the concurrency saved in its state (`state.concurrency`, set from the original `--concurrency`), so the share stays the same. Note this in a code comment.
  - `options.control?: SuiteControl`. After every state change, call `control.setAllowed({ retry: failedNames, integrate: nothingRunningOrQueued && anyDone && anyFailed })`.
  - Race the child exits with `control.next()`:
    - `{retry: name}`: set the feature to `queued` with a flag `resume: true` (keep it in memory only; on disk the existence of its `state.json` decides). Start it when a slot is free.
    - `{integrate: true}`: set every `failed` feature to `excluded`, save, and leave the loop.
  - End of the loop:
    - all non-excluded features done, and at least one done: return `"features-done"`;
    - nothing running or queued, failures left, and no control: suite `failed`, exit 2, and log `run graph-execution suite --resume to retry the failed features`;
    - with a control: keep waiting on `control.next()` (`undefined` means quit, and the suite ends `failed` with exit 2).
  - After `"features-done"`, for now set suite status `done`, log `suite done` plus `excluded: x, y` if any, and exit 0. The next slice replaces this with integration, so keep it in a clearly named function `afterFeatures(ctx)`.
  - On stop (signal), call `control?.quit()` as well.
- **GOTCHA**: never start more children at once than the suite's `concurrency`. Count running children, not features.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx tsc --noEmit`

### UPDATE `src/cli.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: in the `suite` action, when `--resume` is set (from the subcommand or root opts), call `resumeSuite({cwd, suiteId: run})`; otherwise call `runSuite`. With `--resume`, `--feature` must be empty (`UsageError("--resume takes no --feature")`).
- **VALIDATE**: `npx tsc --noEmit && npx eslint src/cli.ts src/suite`

### UPDATE `src/suite/orchestrator.test.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT** (fake provider, real children through `dist/cli.js`):
  - **Resume after a failure:** feature `bad` fails because its fake script fails task `1` three times. Rewrite the fake script so that task succeeds, then run `resumeSuite`. Expected: `bad` resumes (the spawn args contain `--resume --run <runId>`), both features end `done`, and the suite ends `done`.
  - **Retry while another runs:** the good feature hangs (fake `hang` on one of its tasks) and `bad` fails. Call `control.retryFeature("bad")` after `bad` is `failed` and the script is fixed. Expected: `bad` restarts as a resume while the good one is still running. Then stop the suite.
  - **Start integration:** `bad` keeps failing and the other is done. `control.allowed.integrate` becomes true, and `startIntegration()` ends the suite `done` with exit 0, `bad` `excluded` and the log listing it.
  - **Not allowed:** `retryFeature("good")` returns `{ok: false, reason: "not_failed"}`, and `startIntegration()` returns `{ok: false}` while a feature is still running.
  - **Resume of a finished suite** is refused.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run build && npx vitest run src/suite`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `suite --resume` resumes every unfinished feature (resume when its run exists, fresh otherwise) under the same cap, then continues.
- [ ] A failed feature can be retried through `SuiteControl.retryFeature` while other features run.
- [ ] When the others are done and failures remain, `startIntegration` excludes the failed features and the suite moves on. Excluded features are logged.
- [ ] Without a control, a suite with failures ends `failed` (exit 2) and tells you to `--resume`.
- [ ] A live suite can't be resumed twice (lock). A finished suite can't be resumed.
- [ ] Tests pass: `npx vitest run src/suite`

## Validation commands

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit && npx eslint .
npm run build && npx vitest run src/suite
```
